claims.claim: 'Jape' for joke is pretentious and a singularly displeasing word.
claims.source: Asher Gelzer-Govatos, 'The Literary Crimes of George R.R. Martin', The Erstwhile Philistine, 21 Mar 2012
claims.quote: Jape, aside from its pretentiousness, is a singularly displeasing word

claims.claim: 'Mummer's farce' recurs at least ten times in every book.
claims.source: Asher Gelzer-Govatos, 'The Literary Crimes of George R.R. Martin', The Erstwhile Philistine, 21 Mar 2012
claims.quote: the phrase comes up at least ten times in every book

claims.claim: Giving characters speech patterns (Hodor, Reek's rhymes) is admirable but sometimes inexplicable and tedious across chapters.
claims.source: Asher Gelzer-Govatos, 'The Literary Crimes of George R.R. Martin', The Erstwhile Philistine, 21 Mar 2012

claims.claim: The sex scenes are particularly dire and obviously extraneous.
claims.source: Asher Gelzer-Govatos, 'The Literary Crimes of George R.R. Martin', The Erstwhile Philistine, 21 Mar 2012

claims.claim: The prose is what holds Martin back from being a truly great author despite strong storytelling.
claims.source: Asher Gelzer-Govatos, 'The Literary Crimes of George R.R. Martin', The Erstwhile Philistine, 21 Mar 2012
claims.quote: his prose holds him back from being a truly great author

claims.claim: Martin has a knack for vivid, sometimes hallucinogenic description and builds textured scenes of sounds, smells and tastes.
claims.source: Dade Cariaga, 'George RR Martin: American Tolkien?', 19 Sep 2011
claims.quote: textured scenes full of sounds and smells and tastes

claims.claim: For all its vividness the work is pulp with no moral and no depth beneath the diversion.
claims.source: Dade Cariaga, 'George RR Martin: American Tolkien?', 19 Sep 2011

claims.claim: Each new wonder carries a strong whiff of making-it-up-as-he-goes.
claims.source: Dade Cariaga, 'George RR Martin: American Tolkien?', 19 Sep 2011

claims.claim: Watching the HBO series forgoes the great pleasure of Martin's deft prose.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'A Dance with Dragons: A Masterpiece Worthy of Tolkien', Time, 7 Jul 2011
claims.quote: the great pleasure of Martin's deft prose

claims.claim: Like Wagner, Martin gives each character recurring leitmotif phrases in their streams of thought ('You know nothing, Jon Snow', 'If I look back I am lost').
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'A Dance with Dragons: A Masterpiece Worthy of Tolkien', Time, 7 Jul 2011
claims.quote: Like Wagner, he gives each of his characters leitmotifs

claims.claim: Eleven major storylines each have their own rhythm and are written in their own voice, playing off one another.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'A Dance with Dragons: A Masterpiece Worthy of Tolkien', Time, 7 Jul 2011
claims.quote: each with its own rhythm, written in its own voice

claims.claim: Martin will never win a Pulitzer but his skill as a crafter of narrative exceeds almost any literary novelist's.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'A Dance with Dragons: A Masterpiece Worthy of Tolkien', Time, 7 Jul 2011
claims.quote: his skill as a crafter of narrative exceeds

claims.claim: After five volumes Martin is a better writer than when he started.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'A Dance with Dragons: A Masterpiece Worthy of Tolkien', Time, 7 Jul 2011
claims.quote: a better writer than when he started

claims.claim: There is no stock character or cardboard village; every person, wood and street corner has its own tale.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'A Dance with Dragons: A Masterpiece Worthy of Tolkien', Time, 7 Jul 2011
claims.quote: no such thing as a stock character or a cardboard village

claims.claim: The series is an epic for a more profane, sardonic, ambivalent age than Tolkien's.
claims.source: Lev Grossman, 'G.R.R. Martin's Complex Epic for an Ambivalent Age', NPR, 7 Jul 2011
claims.quote: a more profane, more sardonic, more ambivalent age
